# opencode-sessions A plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) V2 that lets any session hand work to your other sessions and hear back. Every top-level session gets tools to list, search, read, start, prompt, watch, open and close other sessions. When a session finishes the work you gave it, only the session that asked is notified. > Supports OpenCode V2 2.2.5 or newer. V1 is not supported.

The demo shows one session handing work to a new session in another repository, the report it gets when that session finishes, and `/go` jumping to the reporting session. ## Features - **Answers "how are we doing with X?"** from the recent conversations of your other sessions. - **Hands work out.** A session sends a prompt to an existing session or starts a new one, then returns at once. It never waits or polls. - **Reports back to the sender only.** If session X hands work to session Y, reports from Y go to X and nowhere else. Each report is a row you can click to open Y, and it starts a new turn in X so X can continue. - **Manages tabs.** New sessions open as tabs, existing ones can be reopened, and a tab can be closed once you say the thread is done. - **Links sessions.** Session IDs in fenced ```` ```session ```` blocks render as clickable links. The tools never answer permissions or questions on your behalf. ## Requirements - OpenCode V2 2.2.5 or newer. ## Install Install the plugin from GitHub with the OpenCode CLI. Pin a release tag: it keeps the install cache stable and lets OpenCode check for updates. ```sh opencode plugin add github:igorovh/opencode-sessions#v0.3.1 ``` This adds the plugin to the global `plugins` array in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`. One entry loads both parts: the server part (the tools and the reports) and the TUI part (tabs, session links and `/go`). Restart OpenCode afterwards. You can also add the entry to the config yourself: ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": ["github:igorovh/opencode-sessions#v0.3.1"] } ``` Update or remove it later: ```sh opencode plugin update github:igorovh/opencode-sessions opencode plugin remove github:igorovh/opencode-sessions ``` ## Getting started Ask any session things like "how are we doing with the checkout launch?" or "start a session in ~/code/app that fixes the flaky login test". When that session finishes, the session you asked gets the report. ## Options `opencode plugin add` does not write options. Add them to the plugin's entry in `opencode.jsonc`: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "github:igorovh/opencode-sessions#v0.3.1", "options": { "scope": "project" } } ] } ``` - `scope`: which sessions the tools can see. `"all"` (default) covers every project. `"project"` limits listing, reading, searching and prompting to sessions of the caller's own project. Directories outside a git repository share one project. These options only reach the server part, which is the only part that uses them. The TUI part has no options. ## Tools The tools work only in top-level sessions (tabs). Subagents get an error, because reports sent to them would never reach you. | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `session_list` | Lists sessions with status: running, idle, or waiting for a permission or an answer. Marks sessions you handed work to or watch. | | `session_search` | Searches titles, prompts and replies of recent sessions for a topic. | | `session_read` | Reads the recent conversation of one session. | | `session_send` | Sends a prompt to a session and returns at once. Your session is notified when that turn ends. | | `session_new` | Starts a new session in a directory with a prompt and opens it as a tab. Your session is notified when its first turn ends. | | `session_open` | Opens an existing session as a tab, or activates its tab if it is already open. Does not change watching. | | `session_close` | Closes a session's tab in every open TUI and ends your watch on it. The session and its history stay. | | `session_watch` / `session_unwatch` | Starts or stops watching every turn of a session, without sending it anything. | Details: - `session_new` switches to the new tab by default. Pass `focus: false` to add the tab in the background, or `open: false` to skip the tab. The result says what the TUI did (for example `TUI: opened and focused.`), or that no TUI confirmed it. - `session_new` and `session_send` accept an optional `model` (`"providerID/modelID"`) and `variant` (for example `"medium"`; requires `model`). The agent passes them only when you name a model; otherwise the project's default model is used. `session_send` switches the session's model before sending, and the switch stays for later turns. - `session_close` refuses while the session is running or waiting for a permission or an answer. - A session has one explicit watcher. `session_watch` from another session replaces it, and `session_unwatch` only removes your own watch. ## Security Prompting another session can make its agent edit files, so `session_send` and `session_new` first check the calling session's `edit` permission for the target directory. With the built-in rules, the Plan agent cannot hand out work, and a build agent with `edit: "ask"` asks you first. To take tools away from every agent, deny them by name in your config, for example: ```jsonc { "permission": { "session_send": "deny", "session_new": "deny" } } ``` Other points: - Reports quote the other session's reply as data, escaped so it cannot close or forge the report block. - `session_read` and `session_search` show the text of other sessions to the calling agent. Use `scope: "project"` if you work in repositories you do not trust. - The server part talks to the local OpenCode service over its HTTP API (`@opencode/client`). It sends nothing anywhere else. ## How it works **Reports.** Each prompt from `session_send` or `session_new` carries `metadata.sessions.from` with the sender's ID. When a turn finishes, fails, is interrupted, or waits for a permission or an answer, the plugin reads that field from the turn and reports to the sender only. A session that `session_watch`es another one also gets reports for turns the user starts there. Everything else reports nowhere. - A turn is everything after the session's previous `idle` message. The plugin pages back up to 5000 messages. - If you type in a tab while another session's prompt waits in the same turn, the whole turn reports to that session. - Each report is a `session.synthetic` message with `delivery: "queue"`, so it never interrupts a running turn. Events within 2 s go into one message, and events for a busy session wait until it is idle. Run `/go` (alias `/inbox`) in a session to pick one of the sessions that reported back to it. **Tabs.** Tabs belong to the TUI, so the server part asks the TUI part to open or close them through RPC events, and each TUI answers through an `ack` method. When session tabs are disabled, opening a tab navigates to the session instead. It works together with [opencode-better-tabs](https://github.com/igorovh/opencode-better-tabs). ## Limitations - A TUI that is not running when a tab event is sent misses it. The tool result then says no TUI confirmed it. - Tabs, session links and `/go` need the plugin in the global config. A plugin added only to a project's `opencode.jsonc` is not loaded by TUIs started in other directories. - `session_search` scans only recent sessions (40 by default, 150 at most) and their recent messages. ## Development Requires [Bun](https://bun.sh). ```sh git clone https://github.com/igorovh/opencode-sessions.git cd opencode-sessions bun install bun run typecheck bun test ``` The TUI part ships precompiled in `dist/tui.js`, because OpenCode does not run the Solid transform for plugins installed from GitHub. After changing `src/tui.tsx` or anything it imports, run `bun run compile` and commit `dist/`; CI fails when it is out of date. `bun run check:dist` checks that both parts import only modules that OpenCode or the plugin's dependencies provide. To run your checkout instead of the published plugin, put its path in `plugins` and restart OpenCode. After that, OpenCode reloads the plugin whenever a file changes. ```jsonc { "plugins": ["/path/to/opencode-sessions"] } ``` The demo GIF is recorded with [VHS](https://github.com/charmbracelet/vhs) from `docs/demo.tape`. It runs OpenCode in a throwaway home with fake repositories and a scripted local model (`docs/demo/mock-model.ts`), so it needs no API key: `DEMO_ROOT= vhs docs/demo.tape`. ## License [MIT](LICENSE)
